cards.term: When the Black Death swept Europe
cards.def: From the late 1340s to the early 1350s the Black Death killed about one-quarter of Europeans, and the resulting labor shortage raised survivors' wages and access to land.

cards.term: When Zheng He's treasure fleet sailed
cards.def: Between 1405 and 1433 Ming China sent Zheng He on seven expeditions, with as many as 300 ships and 28,000 sailors, as far as eastern Africa.

cards.term: Where Europe stood in world commerce around 1450
cards.def: Around 1450 China dominated the world economy, while western Europe remained a poor, divided region on the edge of global trade.

cards.term: When Mehmet II conquered Constantinople
cards.def: In 1453 the Ottomans captured Constantinople, the Christian trading hub between Europe and Asia, deepening European fears for commerce and security.

cards.term: When European monarchs built stronger nation-states
cards.def: After 1450 Henry VII of England, Francis I of France, and Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain expanded royal power, gathering resources for armies, navies, and overseas ventures.

cards.term: When crusaders found sugar plantations
cards.def: After crusaders captured Jerusalem in 1099, Europeans took over its sugar plantations and adopted slave labor because sugar demanded relentless, cheap work.

cards.term: When sugar production moved to Mediterranean islands
cards.def: After Saladin reconquered Jerusalem in the twelfth century, European investors moved sugar plantations to eastern Mediterranean islands, starting sugar's westward march.

cards.term: When Portugal colonized the Atlantic islands
cards.def: In the late 1300s the Portuguese colonized the Canary Islands, and a few decades later Madeira and the Azores.

cards.term: When slave-worked sugar plantations reached the Atlantic islands
cards.def: By the early 1400s the Portuguese had established sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans on the Atlantic islands, a model for later American plantations.

cards.term: When the Portuguese met villagers on the Senegal River
cards.def: In 1455 Portuguese explorers met Senegal River villagers who were curious about European looks but were neither politically nor economically naive.

cards.term: When Columbus took his proposal to Spain
cards.def: In 1485, after Portugal rejected his calculations, Columbus moved to Spain to seek royal support for a westward route to Asia.

cards.term: When Bartolomeu Dias rounded Africa
cards.def: In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope, proving that Portuguese ships could reach the Indian Ocean by sailing around Africa.

cards.term: When Vasco da Gama reached India
cards.def: In 1498 Vasco da Gama reached India by sea, completing Portugal's direct route to Asian markets.

cards.term: When Spain completed the reconquista
cards.def: In 1492 Ferdinand and Isabella captured Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Spain, freeing them to fund Columbus and further expansion.

cards.term: When Columbus first landed in the Americas
cards.def: On October 12, 1492, Columbus landed on San Salvador in the Bahamas, beginning lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.

cards.term: When John Cabot reached North America
cards.def: In 1497 John Cabot, sailing for England, reached the coast near Newfoundland while seeking a northwest passage to Asia.

cards.term: When Spain imposed rule on the Caribbean
cards.def: From the 1490s to the early 1500s Spanish colonizers used warfare, forced labor, and mining against the Taino while Eurasian diseases sped their decline.

cards.term: When Cortés reached Mexico
cards.def: In 1519 Cortés landed on Mexico's Gulf Coast, learned of the Aztec Empire, and recruited its resentful enemies for an inland assault.

cards.term: When smallpox devastated central Mexico
cards.def: In 1520 and 1521 smallpox killed huge numbers of Aztecs, weakening resistance during Cortés's siege of Tenochtitlán.

cards.term: When Tenochtitlán surrendered
cards.def: In August 1521 Tenochtitlán fell to Cortés and his Indian allies, ending Aztec power and giving Spain control of Mexico.

cards.term: When Ponce de León was mortally wounded in Florida
cards.def: In 1521 Indians resisting Juan Ponce de León's Florida expedition mortally wounded him, ending his attempt to colonize Florida.

cards.term: When Pizarro conquered the Incas
cards.def: In 1532 Francisco Pizarro began the conquest of the Inca Empire, extending Spanish rule into South America.

cards.term: When Coronado explored the Southwest
cards.def: From 1540 to 1542 Coronado's expedition crossed the Southwest and the southern Plains seeking rich cities but found none.

cards.term: When Spanish American silver production surged
cards.def: In the 1540s great silver strikes in Mexico and South America turned Spanish conquest into a large-scale capitalist mining enterprise.

cards.term: How large Potosí was by 1570
cards.def: By 1570 the silver-mining city of Potosí in the Andes held about 120,000 people, more than any city in Spain.

cards.term: How much silver Spanish America sent to Europe
cards.def: In the sixteenth century Spanish America shipped about 16,000 tons of silver to Europe, and the Spanish Crown claimed one-fifth of all silver mined.

cards.term: When Luther developed justification by faith
cards.def: Between 1513 and 1517 Martin Luther concluded that salvation was God's free gift received through faith, not a reward earned by good works.

cards.term: When Luther posted his Ninety-five Theses
cards.def: In 1517 Luther publicly attacked the sale of indulgences, turning criticism of Catholic abuses into a movement that challenged Church authority.

cards.term: When independent Lutheran churches formed
cards.def: In the 1520s Luther's followers organized their own churches in Germany, permanently breaking western Europe's Catholic unity.

cards.term: When Calvin published the Institutes of the Christian Religion
cards.def: In 1536 John Calvin published the Institutes of the Christian Religion, spreading his teachings on predestination and the calling across Europe.

cards.term: When the Huguenots first settled in America
cards.def: In 1562 Jean Ribault led French Huguenots to found a settlement on Parris Island, an early attempt at an American refuge that soon collapsed.

cards.term: When the Huguenots founded Fort Caroline
cards.def: In 1564 Huguenots built Fort Caroline in Florida and allied with the Timucua, alarming Spain about French piracy and expansion.

cards.term: When Spain founded St. Augustine
cards.def: In 1565 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded St. Augustine in Florida and destroyed Fort Caroline to block French Protestant expansion.

cards.term: When Gilbert received England's first colonial charter
cards.def: In 1578 Elizabeth I granted Humphrey Gilbert England's first charter to colonize America, but he died at sea before founding a settlement.

cards.term: When Raleigh launched the Roanoke project
cards.def: In 1584 Walter Raleigh received a royal patent, named the land Virginia, and sent settlers whose leaders soon alienated Wingina's people.

cards.term: When the second Roanoke colony arrived
cards.def: In 1587 John White brought 119 settlers, including families, to Roanoke, but supply shortages and Indian hostility soon left the colony vulnerable.

cards.term: When the Spanish Armada threatened England
cards.def: In 1588 Elizabeth kept every ship home to fight the Spanish Armada, delaying John White's return and stranding the Roanoke colonists.

cards.term: When John White found Roanoke deserted
cards.def: In 1590 John White returned to find Roanoke empty, with only the word CROATOAN carved on a post to hint at the colonists' fate.

cards.term: Where England stood in colonization by 1600
cards.def: By 1600, more than a century after Columbus, England still had no permanent American settlement, while Spain dominated most of the Americas.
